summary: Sogyal Rinpoche worked in Buddhist studies, religious studies, and Tibetology. He studied at the University of Delhi, Cambridge, and under teachers including Dudjom Jigdral Yeshe Dorje and Dilgo Khyentse Rinpoche, later founding Rigpa in 1975.
Sohini Sengupta is a doctoral student in Indology at the University of Chicago, where she held a PhD student post in 2024.

Soiku Shigematsu specializes in Buddhist studies. Educated at Tokyo University of Foreign Studies, the University of Tokyo, and Kyoto University, he taught English literature at Shizuoka University (1975–2001) and was a professor at Kansai Medical University (2001–2006).
Sojo Hirano was a Buddhist studies scholar who served as an assistant professor at Hanazono University (attested 1974) and later as head teacher at Zuigan-ji (attested 1992–1996).
Sokatsu Shaku was a Buddhist studies figure who studied under Kōsen Imakita and Soyen Shaku. He founded Ryobokai in 1901, the Ryobokai Dojo of North America in 1906, and Ningen Zen.

Sokei-an Shigetsu Sasaki worked in Buddhist studies. He studied at the Tokyo Academy of Fine Arts, San Francisco Art Institute, and under Sokatsu Shaku and Soyen Shaku. In 1930, he founded the First Zen Institute of America.

Sokichi Tsuda worked in history, archaeology, Sinology, and Japanology. After studying at Tōkyō Senmon Gakkō, he worked at the SMR Research Department (~1908–1919) and held posts at the University of Tokyo and Waseda University (~1920–1940).

Soko Morinaga worked in Buddhist and religious studies. He studied at Daitoku-ji under Zuigan Goto and Sesso Oda. He served as abbot of Daishuin (~1963–1995) and head of Hanazono University (1986–1994).

Sokuo Eto was a Buddhist studies scholar educated at Komazawa University, Kyoto University, and the University of Tokyo. He founded Dokenryo in 1937, became president of Komazawa Junior College (~1950–1958), and was a professor at Komazawa University in 1953.

Solomon Caesar Malan worked in Indology and linguistics. Educated at St Edmund Hall, Oxford, and the University of Edinburgh, he served as classical lecturer at Bishop's College, Calcutta (1838), Secretary of The Asiatic Society (~1838–1840), and Fellow at Balliol College (1843).

Solomon George FitzHerbert specializes in Tibetology and history and archaeology. He earned his doctorate at the University of Oxford, where he was a departmental lecturer, and has worked as a researcher at the National Centre for Scientific Research (attested 2019).
Soma Thera was a Buddhist studies figure who studied at St. Benedict's College, Colombo, and under Jetavana Sayadaw in 1936. He was a member of Servants of the Buddha around 1929.

Somadeva Vasudeva is an Indologist who earned his PhD at the University of Oxford under Alexis Sanderson. He has held positions at Wolfson College, the French Institute of Pondicherry, Columbia University, and Kyoto University.

Somboon Watana specializes in religious studies, Buddhist studies, and philosophy. He completed his PhD at Panjab University under Rekha Jhanji and Dharmanand Sharma in 1999 and became an assistant professor at Mahidol University (attested 2026).

Somchai Kusalacitto works in Buddhist studies and philosophy. He earned a Ph.D. from the University of Madras and served as dean and deputy rector for foreign affairs at Mahachulalongkornrajavidyalaya University (attested 2003).

Somdet Phra Nyanasamvara was a Buddhist studies figure who studied at Wat Bowonniwet Vihara and under Vajirayanavangsa. He served as abbot of Wat Bowonniwet Vihara (~1961–2013) and director of Mahamakut Buddhist University in 1961.
Somphong Santacitto is a Buddhist studies scholar who completed a master's degree at Mahachulalongkornrajavidyalaya University under the supervision of Phra Suthithammanuwat (attested 2006).
Somsak Phansiri is a scholar of Indology, Buddhist studies, and linguistics who earned a PhD at the University of Madras (2005–2011) and serves as a lecturer at Buriram Rajabhat University (2026).

Sonam Chhoki specializes in Tibetology and history and archaeology. She studied at Jawaharlal Nehru University and SOAS University of London, and she has worked as a history teacher at Samtse College of Education.
Sonam Choden works in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. She is a doctoral local researcher and scientific project employee at the University of Hamburg (attested 2026).
